summary.headline: Elgi Q2 FY27: revenue up 17% YoY (about 4 points from FX), EBITDA up 28% to Rs 1,850 mn, margin 16.3% vs 14.9%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 17% YoY, with about 4 points from foreign exchange, and EBITDA rose 28% to Rs 1,850 mn, lifting EBITDA margin to 16.3% from 14.9%. India overperformed ROW, taking a 52:48 revenue mix, and compressors remained about 92% of revenue. Material cost inflation that began in Q2 (Rs 170 mn EBITDA impact) was only partly passed through, with further price corrections expected in Q3. Management flagged metal and fuel inflation and West Asia conflict costs as the key concerns, and said a cost-reduction plan would take 6 to 9 months.

financial_highlights.change: 50-60% recognised in Q2 as credit to material cost; balance in inventory

segments.name: Compressors
segments.commentary: About 92% of overall revenue; mix unchanged. India at 52% and ROW at 48% of sales this quarter.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Strongest growth YoY and sequentially; drivers cited were Demand=Match conversion, a go-to-market project fully in place this FY, and a buoyant Indian economy.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Significant YoY growth and sustained sequential revenue. Industrial business is the profit driver; Pattons still a challenge but service and equipment sales are improving.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Industrial business grew YoY; Italy portables (Rotair) muted due to European economic slowdown and US tariffs on exports. Management guides Europe to marginal profit for FY27, with break-even as the worst case.

segments.name: Australia
segments.commentary: Units business grew well; service slightly muted. Reorganisation under way, with recovery expected in Q3/Q4.

segments.name: Oil-free compressors
segments.commentary: Driven by pharma and food processing; now carved out as a separate vertical in sales; management cites a strong FY27 order book.

segments.name: Vayu (India entry-level range)
segments.commentary: Targets low-cost Chinese imports; about 35% geographic coverage by September, full national coverage targeted by Jan/Feb 2027. Order book and sales above plan; addressable market about 25-30% of oil-lubricated screw compressor volumes.

guidance_outlook: Management expects further metal-price corrections to flow through in Q3, after partial pass-through in Q2; no firm gross margin guidance given for H2.
Europe expected to be marginally profitable in FY27, with break-even as the worst case, conditional on no further geopolitical disruption.
Australia expected to return to track in Q3/Q4 FY27 after reorganisation.
Cost-reduction initiatives covering material, variable and fixed costs; plan expected in 6 to 9 months, with more clarity by Q4 FY27 end.
MK2 campus: first phase (global parts support centre) live; diesel and portable compressor shift to complete by Q1 CY2028, within Rs 600 crore over 4-5 years.
Vayu full national coverage targeted by Jan/Feb 2027.
capex_capacity: MK2 campus programme (about Rs 600 crore over 4-5 years) ongoing; the global parts service warehouse (fully automated) is operational.
Diesel and portable compressor relocation from city factory to main campus: approvals received, work started, completion expected by Q1 CY2028.
Germany entry under way; management says no significant incremental cost, with some revenue-producing roles to be added.
demand_pricing: India growth from Demand=Match conversion, go-to-market project, and economic buoyancy; inquiry levels up.
Brazil growth was lower than last year's post-election bump; Middle East and Africa hit by war-related disruption.
Gross margins in Tier-2 markets (Brazil, Middle East, Africa) are similar to India, with lower price points than Europe, US and Australia.
Metal commodity prices still rising; price increases pushed through to July/August have been partly offset; Q2 increases not yet reflected in pricing.
North America EBITDA described as healthy, with growth driven by aftermarket and volume; no margin-driven change expected.

qa_highlights.question: Harshit Patel: Of the planned price corrections for FY27 (about 9% material cost rise), how much is in the market, and where will gross margin settle in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not give a precise answer. Metal prices are still rising; price increases to July/August were absorbed, but Q2 increases are not yet reflected, with some correction expected in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Harshit Patel: Is Europe still on track for marginal profit and Australia back on track by Q3/Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Europe is expected to be marginally profitable, with break-even the worst case, provided there are no further geopolitical disruptions. Australia reorganisation is on track for Q3/Q4 returns.

qa_highlights.question: Harshit Patel: How is the tariff refund accounted for?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 50-60% of the roughly Rs 40 crore refund was recognised in Q2 as a credit to material cost; the balance sits in inventory and will be realised in Q3/Q4 as stock is sold.

qa_highlights.question: Ankur: Is India growth driven by Demand=Match, the new launches, or the economy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not split it into three buckets. Demand=Match lifted conversion, the go-to-market project increased inquiries, and the Indian economy was buoyant.

qa_highlights.question: Ankur: Will Germany entry add overheads, and what are the margin outlooks for Europe and the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no significant cost increase beyond what is already in P&L. US industrial EBITDA is very healthy and will grow with aftermarket; Europe is a medium-term play.

qa_highlights.question: Manish: Why is Italy loss-making, and what is the Standalone vs consolidated other income gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Italy losses relate to Rotair portables hit by US tariffs and weak European demand; industrial Italy was not an issue. Standalone other income includes subsidiary dividend that is eliminated on consolidation. Last year had a Rs 39 crore property sale gain.

qa_highlights.question: Manish: Why did IT and legal/professional costs rise?
qa_highlights.answer: IT costs cover cybersecurity, a global consolidation and standardisation of services, CRM in India, US and Australia, and some capex moved to leasing and opex. Legal and professional costs were high last year on GTM consulting; no major GTM spend yet this year.

risks_watch: Metal and fuel inflation not yet fully priced in; Q3 margin depends on the timing and size of price corrections.
Geopolitical conflict (West Asia) disrupting Middle East, Africa and Europe; management says Europe is most exposed.
Europe remains loss-making in parts and depends on a recovery in industrial investment; Pattons (US) still weak.
Rising IT, legal and professional costs (consolidated legal and professional about Rs 78 crore) and new cost-reduction plan to be tested in 6-9 months.
Vayu margins will be below the Elgi range at gross level; watch progress towards national coverage by Jan/Feb 2027.
Tariff refund balance (about 40-50% of Rs 40 crore) to be realised in Q3/Q4 and is non-recurring.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume growth and India, and on Europe and Australia returning to profit, but cautious and at times vague on near-term gross margin and metal cost pass-through. Management said it could not give a clear answer on the price corrections, and it flagged inflation as the main concern.
key_quotes: So, I continue to maintain that we are on track for whatever we had guided.
I think overall, there is a positive outlook for EBITDA.
We have taken some proactive steps. It will take us maybe 6 to 9 months to put together a plan

adds.what: MK2 campus first phase: global parts service warehouse (fully automated), operational
Diesel and portable compressor relocation from city factory to MK2 main campus
Vayu India entry-level range: 35% geographic coverage by September, full national coverage targeted by Jan/Feb 2027

growth.why: Q2 revenue grew 17% (about 4 pts from FX) and EBITDA rose 28%, but management gave no firm H2 gross margin or revenue guidance, flagged metal inflation not fully passed through, and Europe guided only to marginal profit; growth is backed by India demand conversion, a strong oil-free order book and Vayu rollout, with capacity mainly the MK2 campus rather than production capacity.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Rs 170 mn material cost headwind in Q2 only partly passed through, metal prices still rising with Q2 increases not yet in pricing, and no firm H2 gross margin guidance, against a Q2 EBITDA margin of 16.3% vs 14.9% a year ago.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: MK2 campus diesel and portable compressor relocation (within about Rs 600 crore over 4-5 years) is under construction with completion by Q1 CY2028, while the parts warehouse is already commissioned, though this is relocation rather than new production capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 revenue grew 17% YoY (about 4 pts from FX), India is 52% of sales and growing fastest on Demand=Match conversion, the oil-free order book is described as strong, and Vayu is above plan, with Brazil and Middle East/Africa the soft spots.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says the capex programme is in line with the ongoing MK2 plan (about Rs 600 crore over 4-5 years) and gives no new capacity announcement, with utilisation not disclosed, so a fresh capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no firm H2 revenue or margin guidance, flagged cost inflation not yet baked in, and Europe is only guided to marginal profit with break-even as the worst case.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Metal and fuel inflation and West Asia costs are not fully priced in, with further price corrections due in Q3 and no clear answer on H2 gross margin, so the risk of a cut is real if pass-through lags.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Vayu entry-level range is at 35% geographic coverage by September with full national coverage targeted by Jan/Feb 2027, and oil-free compressors are now a separate sales vertical with a strong FY27 order book.

rows.label: Europe marginal profit in FY27 (break-even worst case)
rows.why: Management guides Europe to marginal profitability for FY27 with break-even as the worst case, conditional on no further geopolitical disruption, though Italy Rotair portables are muted by European slowdown and US tariffs.

rows.label: Australia recovery in Q3/Q4 FY27
rows.why: Units business grew well and the reorganisation is on track for a return in Q3/Q4, though service is slightly muted.

rows.label: Tariff refund balance realised in H2
rows.why: About 40-50% of the roughly Rs 40 crore US tariff refund sits in inventory and will be realised as stock sells, a non-recurring one-off that flatters the bottom line.

tone.note: Management was confident on India volume growth, Europe returning to marginal profit and Australia recovery, but cautious and vague on near-term gross margin and how much metal cost is passed through; analysts pressed on the price corrections, margin trajectory and the IT and legal cost increases.
